ledger.claim: The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check trips on the driver's own profile, and it trips on both limbs. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 is 0.115, comfortably above the 0.08 threshold. Both of these are fields POL-GEN-01 permits to be cited, and only for this test. The consequence under POL-NS-07 is that the driver's compensation is WITHHELD and the matter escalates - it does not turn on anything about the rider.

Because the POL-NS-07 check trips, POL-NS-09(d) makes escalation to a human reviewer mandatory, and escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal for the automated pipeline: no monetary ruling issues and the disputed SGD 4.00 is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded. The payments ledger already shows exactly that state - payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge while the review is open.

POL-NS-07 does not merely escalate; it requires the escalation packet to DIRECT the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. The refund the rider asks for is therefore the destination the packet must carry once the reviewer opens it, not an open question for the reviewer to work out from scratch.

The escalation is driven entirely by the driver's 30-day termination pattern, not by any abuse on the rider's side. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged. Because escalation REPLACES the monetary outcome, the automated pipeline does not collect the fee from this rider.

All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold on this trip. (a) The trip record carries a driver arrival event at 06:41:20. (b) The trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10, ten seconds before that marker. (c) The driver then held position inside the geofence continuously for 507 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum, the dwell running from the first qualifying in-geofence fix as the clause requires and not from the arrival event. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the required dwell elapsed at 06:46:10. The cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable at the SGD 4.00 fixed by the fee schedule's greater-of rule for a STANDARD pickup in a RYDE_X vehicle.

The POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied with room to spare, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is unassailable. Fifty-two of the driver's fixes are qualifying in-radius fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the qualifying run opens at 06:41:10, before the recorded arrival event. The rider cannot argue the driver never arrived at the pin; the fixes say he did.

There is no waiting-period shortfall for the rider to exploit under POL-NS-06. The effective in-geofence dwell is 507 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum — a surplus of 207 seconds — so the refund-on-shortfall rule never engages. Nor is any traffic advisory needed, because the qualifying hold is a single unbroken run and POL-NS-06(i) accumulation only matters where there are separate intervals to add together. That EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) therefore costs the driver nothing: absence of an advisory is citable but irrelevant where the dwell is already sufficient on its own.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05. At the moment the driver marked arrival his fixes are inside the geofence and stationary — the qualifying run of 52 fixes begins at 06:41:10 and the driver holds position from there — so he was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor travelling at 15 km/h or above when he marked arrival. The recomputation POL-NS-05 performs on a false marker is not required here, and the marker stands as a true one.

POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record. Its limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message sent by the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log holds four entries across 06:41:21 to 06:49:20 — one system 'Your driver has arrived' notice and three messages from the driver — with the rider sending nothing at all. With limb (a) failing, the rider-exoneration clause is out, and the driver's reply conduct under limb (b) is never reached.

The rider's own device track refutes the claim that he came down. Across 118 rider fixes in the window his position sits between 1,894 and 1,907 metres from the pickup pin, never once inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius; his qualifying presence fix count is zero. The rider was not at or near the pickup point at any time during the wait, and his assertion that he was 'a few minutes late' to the kerb is contradicted by the geometry computed from his own device.

Wrong-entrance allocation under POL-NS-03 does not arise. That clause is confined to a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's stationary qualifying fixes are inside the 50 m arrival radius itself. There is no mislocation to apportion between the parties and no pin-ambiguity goodwill to pay out of platform funds.

The driver behaved exactly as the policy expects of a driver kept waiting. He placed an in-app call at 06:45:10 that went unanswered, and sent three in-app messages at 06:42:30, 06:46:02 and 06:49:20 — each delivered and each read by the rider — before cancelling at 06:49:37. This was a patient, documented, eight-and-a-half-minute wait at the correct block, not the speculative cancellation the rider's claim implies.

On a verified rider no-show the driver's compensation is fixed by POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the itemised fee — SGD 3.20 of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee. The fare breakdown's cancellation_fee of 4.00 reconciles with the STANDARD zone-class fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00 under the fee schedule's greater-of rule, so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect arises and the fee line needs no discount.

I cannot argue that counter away, and I do not try to. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: on the merits of the trip itself the driver is right, but the fee cannot be collected and no compensation can be paid, so this case goes to a human reviewer.

The driver waited long enough at the correct place. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00207 (weight 1.0) places his vehicle inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10 and holding position without a break for 507 seconds - a surplus of 207 seconds over the 300 second STANDARD minimum - and the trip record EV-TRIP-00207 (weight 1.0) shows the arrival event at 06:41:20, no boarding event, and termination by the driver at 06:49:37 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the required dwell elapsed at 06:46:10. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable. The supporting clauses raise nothing against it: POL-NS-02 is satisfied by the 52 qualifying in-radius fixes; POL-NS-05 finds no false arrival marker because the driver was inside the geofence and stationary at the marker; POL-NS-06 finds no shortfall, and the MISSING advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) costs nothing because the hold is a single unbroken run needing no accumulation; POL-NS-03 never engages because the driver was inside the arrival radius, not outside it; and POL-NS-04 cannot run because its limb (a) requires a locating message from the rider, and the rider sent nothing - the four chat entries are one system notice and three driver messages (06:42:30, 06:46:02, 06:49:20), all delivered and all read. The rider's own device track sits between 1,894 and 1,907 m from the pin across the whole window, so the account of having come down 'a few minutes late' is contradicted by the geometry from his own phone.

What stops the money is POL-NS-07. Its anti-farming check reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 = 11.5 percent, above the 0.08 threshold. Both limbs are met, so the driver's compensation of SGD 3.20 (80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee) is WITHHELD and POL-NS-09(d) makes escalation to a human reviewer mandatory. Escalation is terminal for the automated pipeline: no refund and no payment issue now, and the disputed SGD 4.00 is held rather than collected from the rider or refunded - the ledger already shows payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

The escalation packet carries one instruction that POL-NS-07 itself requires: direct the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. The open question the reviewer must settle is the driver's trailing-30-day no-show termination pattern, not the events at Blk 682 on 29 July. The rider's own counters are clean - no_show_disputes_30d = 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged - and no rider-side abuse is in issue. The lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter was raised in argument only to be set aside; it is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is read for no test here.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-07: direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full; the disputed fee remains held rather than collected or refunded by the automated pipeline while review is pending.
